Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington’s latest push to stop Europe’s bloodiest conflict since second world war.
The talks in a grand imperial palace in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia – the release of Stephen Hubbard, a retired US teacher held in Russia.
President Donald Trump confirmed the release in a social media post, saying the United States was not required to give anything in return.
Hubbard was first detained in April 2022 and was later sentenced to six years and 10 months on charges whose veracity his family and US-based lawyer question.

articles.title_orig: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
articles.title_zh: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
articles.content_orig:
Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago.
The penalty, revealed in a court filing, comes after a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse found in September the social media giant liable for misleading state citizens about how it safeguards and collects user data and prevents harmful information from flourishing on its services.
Although the jury concluded that Meta had over 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices act, with each transgression carrying a civil penalty as high as $5,000, a New Mexico judge was responsible for determining the ultimate fine. The Wednesday filing showed that the state was awarded $219.5 billion, but the penalty was ultimately reduced to $25 billion.
"The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook's repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury," New Mexico district court judge Francis Mathew wrote in the filing.
The judge added that interest on the penalty shall accrue at the rate of 15% each year until the fine is paid off in full.
CNBC has reached out to Meta for comment on the penalty order.
Meta previously resolved various Cambridge Analytica-derived data privacy lawsuits across the nation as part of an overarching August settlement of nearly $17 billion with a coalition of state attorneys general in a separate federal case related to child safety and mental health. But because New Mexico was not part of the settlement, the state's data privacy case that arose from Meta's Cambridge Analytica scandal proceeded to trial in September.
In 2022, the social media giant agreed to pay $725 million to settle a class action lawsuit that also sprang from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal that kicked off in 2018. That scandal rocked the Mark Zuckerberg-led company before its official name change to Meta, and focused on allegations that the political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica improperly accessed the information of 87 million users , raising questions about Facebook's data handling practices.
Judge Mathew said in the filing that "Facebook did not conduct the comprehensive investigation that it promised" following the Cambridge Analytica revelations.
"Pressure from senior executives to keep costs down, lack of adequate enforcement resources, inadequate investigative techniques, and a desire not to create precedent for future investigations," all contributed to what the judge characterized as a "willfully ineffective" internal examination by Facebook, the filing said.
Former New Mexico state Attorney General Hector Balderas originally filed the state's Cambridge Analytica-related lawsuit in 2021, while current AG Raúl Torrez oversaw the related trial.
Torrez also led his state's child-safety related trial against Meta that resulted in a March jury ruling that the social media company should pay $375 million for violating the state's unfair practices act. A New Mexico judge would later order Meta to pay $567 million into an abatement fund as part of a second phase of the case that determined the social media firm's actions created a public nuisance.
Meta said it disagreed with that New Mexico ruling and planned to appeal.

SpaceX ( SPCX ) just opened with its biggest jump since the company's June debut and is on pace for its best day in two months. Its space stock followers are also bouncing, but from a much deeper hole.
SpaceX gapped higher after its third quarter revenue and profit topped Wall Street's estimates . Its AI business now brings in nearly half the company's sales . CEO Elon Musk said late Tuesday that SpaceX and Tesla ( TSLA ) have both formed committees to study a merger . Tesla reports after Wednesday's close.
Through Tuesday, SpaceX stock was down just 2% in October, while the typical newer space stock was down about 26%. Legacy defense names such as Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) and Northrop Grumman ( NOC ) mostly gained.
SpaceX hasn't moved in step with its space peers since its debut, by Yahoo Finance calculations, even as the rest of the group has traded almost as one.
In early trading on Wednesday, every newer space stock is higher. Intuitive Machines ( LUNR ) and Firefly Aerospace ( FLY ) are among the leaders, while Rocket Lab ( RKLB ) and AST SpaceMobile ( ASTS ) trail.
Not everyone will cheer the spending. SpaceX's plan to spend $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter "suggests a new and higher level of capex than the market expected," Chris Versace of Tematica Research wrote Wednesday, though he noted it's backed by a $63 billion backlog.
SpaceX's first trade after its IPO came at $150, and bulls initially treated that price as a line in the sand. Below it, $140 became recent support — a floor where buyers keep stepping in — through August and September.
October's pullback stalled well above that floor, with closes holding in the $146-$148 range last week. Wednesday's gap carried the stock past $160 in one jump.
Overhead, closes stalled near $172 in late June and again in early October. That's potential resistance , where sellers have reloaded before. Above it, the June highs around $210 are the next potential wall.
Holding $150 keeps Wednesday's gap intact. A break back below puts $140 in focus, then the $135 IPO price. Bulls first need a close above $172 to put $210 in view.
The next test comes fast. Up to 1.3 billion shares unlock on Thursday , the biggest share release yet, though past unlocks have barely dented the stock. The largest, in August, came right at the low.
Watch whether SpaceX holds its gap into the close. If it can stay above $150 through Thursday's unlock, buyers are absorbing the new supply comfortably.

articles.title_orig: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
articles.title_zh: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
articles.content_orig:
Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors say
Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping .
Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has vowed to take by force if necessary.
In one performance, Huang Yi-hao insulted the Chinese leader’s appearance, compared him to Winnie-the-Pooh and tore into his political record.
Prosecutors in New Taipei said on Wednesday that an individual from mainland China who was identified as “K” had paid the five defendants to injure Huang badly enough to require hospitalisation.
The prosecutors said: “This case involves a serious incident in which the Chinese Communist party is suspected of using cross-border suppression tactics to direct lawless elements in our country to suppress dissenting political voices through extreme violence.”
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to requests for comment.
A GPS tracker was allegedly put on Huang’s scooter months before the attack to identify his daily routines, Taiwan’s Central News Agency said. On 11 September, two defendants drove into Huang’s bike as he rode home, but stopped after hearing Huang scream, prosecutors said.
The comedian was left with a bruised pelvis and the suspects then allegedly pretended to help with an insurance claim in order to send a photo of Huang’s medical certificate to K.
K refused to pay the full sum of NT$450,000 (US$13,900; £10,370) promised to the suspects because Huang’s injuries were only minor, the statement said.
On Wednesday, Huang reposted a video from December 2025 in which he asked the audience to help him by shouting out the name of the person he was about to describe.
In a fast-paced diatribe, the comedian, dressed in a traditional gown, evoked “swept-back hair” and a “plump figure”, and criticised policies on Hong Kong, Covid and the property market. After finishing with an expletive, the crowd chanted back Xi’s name before breaking into applause.
In May, two people were prosecuted after spreading faeces and paint at a Taipei club hours before a Huang show.
Lev Nachman, a professor of political science at National Taiwan University, said: “It is important to remember that what we are reading about is obviously a more extreme case, but there have been threats and acts of violence against critics of the Communist party here in Taiwan for many years.”
Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council said in October that at least 126 individuals had been affected by Chinese transnational repression.
The Guardian has contacted the Chinese foreign ministry for comment.
In a post on Wednesday, Huang said: “If people can be subjected to this kind of treatment simply for criticising the Chinese Communist party when it does not even govern Taiwan, how can we expect to retain our current freedom of speech if the CCP were ever to rule Taiwan?”
In another post on Facebook, Huang said he would not cancel future performances but that he was “no hero”.
“I write it because it’s funny,” he said. “If I stop, it will only be because I’ve got bored of it.”

articles.title_orig: Meta earnings live updates: AI spending, ad revenue and stock reaction
articles.title_zh: Meta earnings live updates: AI spending, ad revenue and stock reaction
articles.content_orig:
Meta is slated to report third-quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, and investors will be looking for signs that the company's latest artificial intelligence efforts will bolster future sales.
Here's what analysts polled by LSEG are expecting:
It's been a big quarter for Mark Zuckerberg's company due to the initial success of the Muse AI personal assistant tool that debuted in September and shot to the top of Apple's iOS app store. That AI momentum helped Meta end September with its best month on Wall Street since 2022.
Meta isn't the first to create a digital assistant that can organize people's email and scan the web for headphone deals, but the company's empire, which includes Facebook and Instagram, has helped introduce AI agents to the masses. At the same time, Meta and its AI chief Alexandr Wang have continued rolling out new foundation models and related updates at a speedy clip, including Muse Wonder , which was released last Monday.
Wall Street will likely be monitoring for whether Meta plans to increase its data center-related capital expenditures, or capex, to further develop the underlying computing infrastructure needed to power AI agents and foundation models.
The company revealed in July during its second-quarter earnings that it narrowed its 2026 capex guidance to come in between $130 billion and $145 billion, representing a $5 billion increase to the low end of its prior range. All that spending resulted in Meta's free cash flow in the period shrinking to $784 million from $8.55 billion in the same quarter a year earlier.
Analysts expect Meta's capex to swell to $196.3 billion in 2027, according to FactSet.
Meta's third-quarter daily active people, or DAP, is expected to come in at 3.65 billion, according to StreetAccount, almost flat from the prior quarter. That figure represents all of Meta's users across its family of apps like Facebook and Instagram.
Analysts at Bank of America wrote in a note published Friday that they expect Meta to post a sales beat, with revenue of $63.8 billion, based in part on the firm's "solid ad checks" with brands and companies that helps determine the health of the digital ad market.
The analysts don't expect Muse to contribute significantly to Meta's overall business for the rest of this year and 2027 and instead "will consume capacity w/o near-term revs.," meaning that the company's AI agent efforts will take some time to grow into something bigger.
Morgan Stanley analysts agree that Meta's Muse AI agent initiatives won't generate big sales anytime soon, and while they said in a Sunday research note that they are "bullish," they "encourage investors to keep reasonable adoption rates in perspective."
The analysts explained that it takes a long time for new technology habits and behaviors to normalize. In 2000, when the e-commerce boom was just five years deep, for instance, the analysts noted that online retail "only made up 4% of adj retail sales" while adding that "even ~30 years in ('26) it's still only 28%."
Meta will be the first hyperscaler to reveal quarterly financials during this tech earnings cycle, with Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon slated to report next week.
The four companies combined have called for roughly $730 billion in capital expenditures this year as they stock up on graphics processing units and AI systems and look to build massive data centers around the globe .
Analysts polled by FactSet expect that number to hit around $1 trillion next year, led by Alphabet, which is projected to spend over $310 billion. The stepped up spending comes as interest rates soar and concerns intensify that AI revenue won't justify the costs.
Alphabet and Microsoft are scheduled to report earnings next Wednesday, followed by Amazon on Thursday.
Meta's past quarter wasn't all AI agents and good vibes.
The social media giant agreed in August to pay nearly $17 billion to settle a major lawsuit involving a group of state attorneys general, including California's Rob Bonta. The trial centered around allegations that Meta misled the public about the true scope of child mental health related harms caused by certain design elements of apps like Facebook and Instagram , including recommendation algorithms.
Meta's state AG settlement could cause the company to miss on third-quarter earnings per share due to the related $10 billion legal charge that "the street has not yet accounted for," Wolfe Research analysts wrote in a Monday note.
The company still faces numerous personal injury claims and a separate federal case involving a group of nationwide school districts that also focus on allegations that apps like Instagram have had detrimental effects on the well being of children.

articles.title_orig: What We Saw at Fast-Track Trials of Riot Suspects in France
articles.title_zh: What We Saw at Fast-Track Trials of Riot Suspects in France
articles.content_orig:
Nationalist leaders are framing unrest as consequence of failed liberal governance and open borders
Europe’s far-right leaders have jumped on the violence that rocked numerous cities last weekend, framing it as the inevitable consequence of failed liberal governance and open-border policies and insisting only they can restore law and order.
Months away from key elections in Spain, France and Italy, authoritarian nationalists are eager to weaponise the wave of street unrest, originating in peaceful protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services but hijacked by violent rioters.
Those in opposition have not held back. In France, where cities such as Paris, Marseille and Lyon faced widespread rioting and looting, the far-right National Rally (RN) has denounced centrist incompetence and promised a crackdown.
The party’s president, Jordan Bardella, said the government was “impotent”. The RN leader, Marine Le Pen , said on Wednesday the state was “collapsing” and had “lost control of everything” amid “migratory, budgetary and security chaos”.
Ahead in presidential polls and seeking voters beyond her base, Le Pen has resisted explicitly racialising the unrest, but has framed it more broadly as a result of state and policy failures leading to “anarchic immigration” and “a total loss of authority”.
In Germany – where there were no major protests – the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has stoked fears rioting could spill over the border. Its co-leader Alice Weidel said France’s “violent excesses” were a “warning for Germany”.
Weidel also linked the unrest to immigration, posting: “The dangerous mix of mass migration and leftwing extremism threatens to lead to civil war-like conditions here too … There will only be a turnaround on migration with the AfD!”
In Portugal, populists have used peaceful protests to blame immigration for the country’s housing crisis, which André Ventura of the far-right Chega party said was chiefly a consequence of an “uncontrolled influx of people from abroad”.
In Spain, where the housing crisis has led to huge protests and a Madrid encampment, and prompted the socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, to call a snap election next month, the far-right Vox party has sought to demonise the protesters. “They’re not defending the right to housing, or asking for work, they’re serving Pedro Sánchez,” the party’s leader, Santiago Abascal, said. “They’re Sánchez’s militias.”
Vox has also attempted to link the housing issue to migration. In a message posted on social media last month, the party falsely suggested that the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked the mammoth protests would have had a home had she been an immigrant from north Africa.
In Belgium , where cost of living protests also escalated into street clashes in Brussels and Liège, the far-right Flemish nationalists of Vlaams Belang framed the rioting as a failure of integration and open borders, characterising it as “imported violence”.
Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni , has adopted another strategy – as head of a far-right government she has headed for four years, she cannot simply blame failures of the state. Instead, she has expanded her law-and-order agenda, and framed rioters as extremists.
“Demonstrating is a right, but setting our cities ablaze is not,” Meloni said after rioting in Milan and Bologna. “Hooligans have exploited the protests to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security, and hold entire cities hostage.”
after newsletter promotion
Meloni has previously enacted sweeping security measures aimed at hindering public dissent, including jail terms for blocking roads, tough sentences for resisting police officers, and pre-detention for demonstrators thought likely to cause trouble.
This week she passed emergency decrees creating an offence of violent participation in ⁠a demonstration, imposing tougher penalties on ⁠rioters and organisers of violent groups, and penalising parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.
But she too has highlighted immigration as a factor, noting that “nearly half of those stopped or arrested” after the Milan riots were “of immigrant background, including individuals born abroad and second-generation children of immigrant families”.
Beyond Europe’s orthodox far-right parties, anti-immigration polemicists have gone further, interpreting the violence not as state and policy failures but as evidence of a looming civilisational war fuelled by multiculturalism and non-EU immigration.
Éric Zemmour, the founder of France’s Reconquête! (Reconquest) party, demanded an immigration halt and the deportation of “foreign delinquents”, declaring: “These are not riots, but the warning shots in an ethnic war. Either we establish absolute order or we yield.”
The far-right narrative has been reinforced by similar comments from the US, where both the president and vice-president have sought to turn the unrest in France in particular into a cautionary tale for voters before midterm elections.
Donald Trump described France as a once-great nation that had been “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”, adding on social media that immigration “has shattered that once great country”.
JD Vance echoed the same view, saying: “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion.” In doing so, they “ignored fundamental questions about assimilation and compatibility”, he said.
Deborah Cole in Berlin, Angela Giuffrida in Rome and Sam Jones in Madrid contributed reporting

"How you perform indoors, of course, is extremely important, and we shouldn't think about those as being nominal loads," he said. "They're significant loads, even with robust Wi-Fi networks that are out there."

Apple Music has officially launched its rebrand with a new design, logo, and more. And in a video detailing the rebrand, Apple reveals the new look was actually “made by sound.”

articles.title_orig: Nearly $1 million worth of rare Pokemon and sports cards stolen from FedEx truck in Orange County heist, police say
articles.title_zh: Nearly $1 million worth of rare Pokemon and sports cards stolen from FedEx truck in Orange County heist, police say
articles.content_orig:
SANTA ANA, Calif. (KABC) -- Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards, including highly valued Pokémon cards, were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near an Orange County business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.
The theft is the latest in a string of heists involving Pokémon cards, which have exponentially increased in value in recent years.
The Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement on Tuesday that the heist occurred on Oct. 13 outside the Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) office in Santa Ana.
The hundreds of stolen cards are estimated to be worth a total of $963,000, according to police.
"However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined," according to the Santa Ana police statement.
The cards belong to collectors from across the country who submitted them to the PSA to be authenticated and graded.
Two full pallets of collectible cards were stolen, and some cards on a third pallet were also swiped when thieves broke into a FedEx truck, according to police.
"The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokémon cards," according to the police statement.
Thieves carve hole through drywall to steal high-value Pokémon cards from Anaheim shop
As of Wednesday, no arrests have been announced in the memorabilia rip-off. Police said the investigation is ongoing.
"The value is definitely there," said Gregory Lawrence of Shiny Vault Pokémon Cards. "It's another asset class now. It's not just stocks, bonds, and putting money in the bank. You can put money into cards. Whether it's Pokémon or sports, there is a huge following from across the world."
The theft was first reported by The Athletic, which cited police sources saying the the FedEx truck was broken into during the 60 to 90 minutes the driver was away from the parked vehicle.
"We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items. We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues," Collectors, the parent company of PSA, said in a statement to ABC News.
The company said it deactivated the certificates for the missing cards and has notified its "marketplace partners to be on the lookout for rare and serialized items."
"Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value," the company said. "We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset."
FedEx released a statement to ABC7, saying, "The security of our customers' shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation. Further questions should be referred to local investigators."
One victimized collector, known by his online handle, Sky-B Cards, issued a YouTube video statement , saying the 104 cards he submitted to PSA for grading were among the stolen items. He said he paid more than $8,000 to have the cards graded by PSA and that his cards were insured for more than $150,000.
"These were 104 cards that I've accumulated over two years," Sky-B Cards said in the YouTube video. "There are many irreplaceable cards in here that I will never see again, and honestly that's what hurts the most, outside of being absolutely financially destroyed here."
The heist is the latest in a string of thefts in Southern California and elsewhere in the country of highly valued Pokémon cards, highlighting what appears to be an ever-growing demand for merchandise from the popular childhood card game.
In February, thieves broke into a collectibles shop in Anaheim, by cutting a hole through the wall from a neighboring shop they also broke into, stealing tens of thousands of dollars worth of Pokémon cards.
Captured on video surveillance cameras, the three thieves were seen grabbing hundreds of trading cards and bolting from the shop in less than 10 minutes.
In April, thieves staged a smash-and-grab heist at Elite Sports Cards in Chicago, stealing $100,000 in Pokémon cards, the store owner told ABC Chicago station WLS.
In an interview in April, Jared Mast, president of Mast Wealth Management Group, which deals in alternative investments including collectibles like Pokémon cards, told ABC News the value of Pokémon cards has risen sharply in the past year.
"I would say, collectively, over the last 12 months, things have gone up anywhere from 200 to 300%," Mast said.
Mast explained that Pokémon card value has risen in three different waves over the last decade. First, in 2016, with the arrival of Pokémon Go, the popular mobile game based on the playing cards, and then again in 2019 and 2020, as a generation of celebrities like Logan Paul invested in the collectibles.
ABC News contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Websites taken down across Europe as critical cyber-security update issued
articles.title_zh: Websites taken down across Europe as critical cyber-security update issued
articles.content_orig:
International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet.
The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon.
Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline.
The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape.
Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities.
The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix.
"These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote.
Meanwhile, the White House said federal agencies were working with leading AI labs to speed up a fix to the issue.
And in a post on X , Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP.
The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities.
"We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said.
That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday.
Edinburgh council's website has also become inaccessible, as well as the online homes for several BBC programmes including Doctor Who and The Traitors.
They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment.
Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance " without specifying the reason.
The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. They used state-of-the art AI, made by OpenAI, to find the flaws.
OpenAI said in a blog post it was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
According to the firms, they had gone undetected for more than a decade.
"Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post.
It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure.
The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website.
Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.
"Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note .
Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning .
"PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said.
Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers.
The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said.
"The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said.
He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold".
The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution".
Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.
Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up".
The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP".
It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004.
The PHP Foundation has issued the update only for the latest versions however - with people using PHP 8.1 or older being urged to upgrade.
PHP was created for web development. It is used on servers to implement what you see when you visit websites.
Not all websites use it, but it nonetheless powers a large portion of the internet.

articles.title_zh: AMD Announces FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X/S, Z2 Extreme and Z2A Handhelds, RX 6000 GPUs and More
articles.content_orig:
Earlier this month AMD senior vice president Jack Huynh told media in South Korea that FSR 4 was coming to more devices, including handhelds - and now that promise has been fulfilled.
Huynh today announced that FSR 4.1 was coming to five new platforms: Radeon RX 6000-series graphics cards; Gorgon Halo and Strix Halo mini PCs and mobile workstations; Gorgon Halo and Strix Halo Ryzen 9 laptops; Z2 Extreme and Z2A handhelds like ROG Xbox Ally devices; and Xbox Series X and Series S.
It's a welcome surprise to see AMD's latest generation upscaler on a huge range of extra devices - even though community modders have been working hard to port the technique to an even longer list of supported platforms.
FSR 4, previously known as Project Redstone, is AMD's first machine learning upscaler and offers a significant visual advantage over its earlier efforts at similar frame-rates - hence the interest in making it available on a wider range of PCs, handhelds and other devices. As well as upscaling and anti-aliasing, the tech also includes frame generation and ray reconstruction, giving it better feature parity with Nvidia's similar DLSS tech.
Huynh's announcement also states that FSR is coming to Vulkan, a graphics API that is the default choice for games that don't use (or want to offer an alternative to) DirectX 12. FSR 3 and earlier supported Vulkan, so it's good to see this limitation redressed - though it's not clear how quickly developers will be able to add FSR 4.1 support to their Vulkan games.
More APUs will get FSR 4.1 support in the future, Huynh claimed, and the announcement video also mentions that AMD's next-gen FSR Diamond will be supported on Xbox's Project Helix " family of devices ".
If you want to use FSR 4.1 on your PC (officially) for the first time, you'll need to install Adrenalin Edition version 26.10.1 . The graphics drivers also add support for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Final Fantasy Resonance.

The independent MP Helen Haines has lost both legs but remains in a stable condition, two days after an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria.
Haines, the federal MP for Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries.
Her husband, Phil Haines, provided an update on his wife’s condition at Melbourne’s Alfred hospital late on Wednesday afternoon.
Composed and clear, he said his wife had survived a “horrendous incident” and faced a long road to recovery.
“The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she’s stable,” he said.
“That is the most important thing for our family. And I think when we reflect and talk about and think about Helen, the two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind.
“Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person. Incredibly supportive of all around her – her family, her community, anybody she comes across. And her mind. She has the sharpest intellect.”
Phil Haines described his wife, 65, as a fighter. The pair have been married for nearly 40 years and have three children and two grandchildren. He became emotional for a moment at the end of the statement, reflecting on his wife’s strength.
“She is a determined person who will do her best with our support and love to recover, and that is what we hope for,” he said.
“We are grateful at this stage that both her heart and her mind are in good shape.”
Haines asked for donations to Save the Children as his wife recovers. A special appeal has been launched by the charity.
Police allege Monday’s attack was targeted, and have charged Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.
Nugent faced Wangaratta magistrates court earlier on Wednesday.
Phil Haines was joined by the governor general, Sam Mostyn. Mostyn said she had relayed news of the incident to King Charles and praised Helen Haines’s work as a local representative, including her commitment to improving the standards of public discourse in Australia.
“This violent attack on a much loved and respected sitting member of our federal parliament must be a moment for us to pause and to choose to be better,” she said.
“We’ve got to hope that that beautiful heart, that beautiful mind will be strengthened every day by our support and our commitment to be more like Helen as part of this great democracy.”
Anthony Albanese and politicians from across federal parliament have expressed shock and anger at the alleged attack on Haines.
The incident has sparked calls for changes to politicians’ safety, with security services including the Australian federal police and Asio briefing MPs on the current landscape on Wednesday.
Speaking at a vigil in Wodonga on Wednesday evening, Cathy McGowan, who held the seat of Indi before Haines, paid tribute to her friend.
“There is another level of grief, different and deeper from the actual violence, from the sorrow, the shame and the hurt,” she said.
“It’s about Helen in her role as our elected representative. In attacking her, we intuit that this is an attack on our political system, on our democracy, and especially so for all the supporters who did the democracy work getting Helen elected.”
McGowan called for the upcoming Victorian state election campaign to be conducted in a positive and constructive way. Voters go to the polls next month.
The community could not let violence win, McGowan implored.
“That we ensure the legacy of this attack on Helen will be a stronger, more vibrant and effective democracy, and from a personal perspective, all candidates and especially women, know they can run for office and be safe.”

articles.title_orig: China’s Free A.I. Models Are Thrown Into Uncertainty
articles.title_zh: China’s Free A.I. Models Are Thrown Into Uncertainty
articles.content_orig:
As Washington ramps up efforts to tighten cross-border life sciences deals involving Chinese assets, Beijing is moving to tighten its own grip on biomedical innovation, rolling out a draft policy that would ban or restrict the export of key biopharmaceutical technologies.
In a proposed update to its export blacklist published (Chinese) Friday, China’s government revealed that it is looking to block foreign acquisitions of proprietary cell and gene therapy, small interfering RNA (siRNA) and pathogen gain-of-function platforms. In this case, platforms are defined as sets of reusable technologies that can support the development of multiple drugs.
In parallel, the new rule would restrict the full transfer of proprietary drug target identification and verification technologies in the fields of cell and gene therapy and siRNA to entities overseas. Unlike a full-on ban, a restriction would mean that such deals would require regulatory approval.
Biopharma assets are among 40 key technologies being targeted by the government’s update, which also covers AI and photovoltaic green energy.
The proposed policy comes as China has become a leading exporter of biomedicines. According to China’s drug regulators, foreign transactions of Chinese biotech assets reached $120 billion as of August this year, marking a 36% jump year over year.
However, the draft rule’s real impact on Chinese biopharma transactions may be limited.
For biopharma deals, the new regulations can be summarized as “regulating transfers while leaving licensing unconstrained,” Aaron Gu, a partner at Chinese law firm Han Kun that specializes in healthcare and life sciences, told Fierce.
While keen on keeping ownership of key proprietary technologies within China’s borders, the proposed export ban explicitly excludes several common business development types. Out-licensing agreements, as well as utilizing know-how to provide outsourced research and manufacturing services, do not fall under the ban, a spokesperson for China’s Ministry of Commerce highlighted in a media Q&A (Chinese).
Similarly, out-licensing of drug target identification and verification techs will generally be approved, the spokesperson added.
That describes nearly all Western deals for Chinese biotech assets so far. Despite a surge in deal count and value, U.S. and European biopharma companies and venture capitalists have almost exclusively focused on buying specific drugs from their Chinese counterparts or utilizing a platform to identify new molecules. Rarely has ownership of a platform changed hands.
As of July 1, only five of all 121 cross-border Chinese biopharma out-licensing deals this year involved ownership transfer, according to local biopharma data intelligence service provider PharmCube.
One deal that would likely not have been possible under the proposed new rule was AstraZeneca’s $1 billion acquisition of Gracell Biotechnologies , which developed the FasTCAR platform for making CAR-T cells. When announced at the end of 2023, the deal was hailed as the first full acquisition of a Chinese biotech by Big Pharma.
Explaining the government’s rationale in the Q&A, the spokesperson framed the proposal as supporting the “orderly international collaboration around China’s biopharma technologies.” As for the pathogen-related component, the spokesperson cited national security reasons.
Rumors started circulating in May that the Chinese government was looking to slam the brake on biopharma platform acquisitions. At the time, an alleged Ministry of Commerce blacklist circulating online also proposed platform bans on other popular modalities such as multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates and protein degraders.
The Chinese government had been surveying research institutions and biopharma companies over the past two years, trying to get a better grasp of the field’s technology landscape, a senior Chinese biopharma executive told Fierce in an interview in June.
The assessment was launched in response to concerns over the practice of out-licensing or selling early-stage drug candidates—coined by locals as “selling green shoots”—because Chinese biotechs lack the experience or the cash to run late-stage clinical trials and global commercialization, the person said.
“What authorities don’t want to see is someone taking China’s resources to build a great R&D engine, only to sell the entire company overseas, because then China ends up losing the capabilities,” the exec said, commenting on the rumor.
“But if you structure it as a partnership, I’m still the owner,” the exec added. “You’re simply licensing it out so foreign companies can develop it overseas while paying you royalties and milestone payments. I don’t think the Chinese government is against that kind of arrangement.”
“Many of these deals retain rights for China—meaning it won’t impact the development and commercialization of these drugs domestically, so Chinese patients still get access to world-class medicines,” the exec continued. “Second, Chinese companies can gain financial returns through these deals, generating foreign exchange for the country. If you think about it from these angles, that’s really the underlying rationale.”
Now, the published draft policy is “significantly better than market expectations,” Gu of Han Kun said.
The previous rumored list “spanned nearly all the most prominent frontiers of Chinese biopharma business development deals,” he observed. “The market had widely feared that Chinese cross-border dealmaking would suffer a sweeping blow.”
“By deliberately excluding out-licensing structures, the government has clearly taken into account biopharma dealmaking norms and the momentum of cross-border collaboration, reflecting strong support from a policy standpoint,” Gu said.
The Chinese government is seeking comments on the proposed new rule until Nov. 15. Foreign buyers should exercise due diligence regarding this draft policy, Gu said. He noted that, before the revised export control catalogue is officially enacted, any export of technologies falling within the regulated scope must register with the Ministry of Commerce.
Beijing is tightening controls over foreign biopharma transactions just as Washington’s China hawks intensify efforts to curb the American purchase of Chinese biotech assets. articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.content_orig:
On SpaceX's earnings call late Tuesday, CEO Elon Musk , who also runs Tesla , took a break from talking about financial results to tell investors that it would be a "good idea" to merge his two companies, and said the boards at both have formed special committees to discuss a possible tie-up.
Musk will be back in public after market close on Wednesday, this time to discuss Tesla earnings.
Here's what Wall Street is expecting, according to estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:
Should Tesla fail to top expectations, the company would see a slight decrease in revenue from $28.1 billion a year earlier. Tesla has recorded double-digit growth in each of the two prior quarters, but revenue dropped in three of four quarters in 2025, as Chinese EV makers such as BYD and Xiaomi gained popularity in Asia and Europe with affordable and innovative EVs. Tesla was also hit last year by the end of a federal EV tax credit.
Earlier this month, Tesla reported vehicle deliveries for the third quarter of 486,532, about 2% below the year-ago number. Deliveries are the closest approximation of sales reported by Tesla but are not precisely defined in its shareholder communications.
While Tesla still counts on auto sales for the bulk of its revenue, Musk sees the company's future in robotaxis and humanoid robots. That's putting the focus on capital expenditures, which are expected to top $25 billion this year, based on a prior forecast, up from about $8.5 billion in 2025.
One of Tesla's big investments is in a semiconductor factory that it's building with SpaceX and Intel in Grimes County, Texas. That partnership with SpaceX along with other areas of overlap, including work on Tesla's recently announced Roadster refresh, fueled intensifying speculation that Musk's companies were on the verge of combining in what would be a historic transaction.
"I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield," Musk said on the SpaceX earnings call, responding to a question about a potential merger.
"Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said. "But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this." On the Tesla side, that means needing a 50% vote of all shares, which is "quite a high hurdle," he said.
Musk pointed to the company's potential to cooperate on AI software, chip design, Terafab and robotics. Tesla is already using Grok AI technology, developed by SpaceX, to power AI assistants in customer cars, and to help control the company's Optimus humanoid robots now in development.
Tesla's stock price is down 14% this year, after rallying on Wednesday, underperforming all of its megacap tech peers. SpaceX went public in June, and is up from its $150 IPO price after its post-earnings pop.
Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja told investors on the company's last earnings call in July that automotive margins had been challenged this year by rising interest rates and energy costs.
But he also touted growing revenue from Full Self-Driving (Supervised), sometimes referred to as FSD, the partially automated driving system Tesla sells for $99 per month. FSD doesn't make Tesla vehicles safe to use without a human driver, and the company markets the system as Assisted Driving in Europe. Taneja said Tesla reached close to 1.5 million paid FSD customers globally as of the end of June.
Investors submitted questions online ahead of Wednesday's call, and one of the top-voted requests was for updates on FSD and when it could become "unsupervised," making customers' vehicles fully automated and safe to use like a robotaxi.
Shareholders also want to hear an update on Tesla's Cybercab, a bronze two-seater designed for use as a robotaxi, but not yet sold to individuals.
Tesla is testing the Cybercab, and has deployed driverless vehicles in a limited U.S. fleet. But the company still lags far behind Alphabet's Waymo in the U.S., and Baidu's Apollo Go in China.

articles.content_orig:
Google’s Face Unlock feature on Pixel phones works really well, until the lights go out. The company appears to be building out a new upgrade to this with “active illumination” which is… just turning up the screen brightness.
Face Unlock as it exists on Pixel 8 and newer relies on the camera and Google’s software to deliver biometric authentication that’s actually strong enough to let you unlock secure apps such as banking and password manager apps.
While the fingerprint sensor serves as a fine backup, not having Face Unlock in dark rooms can be a tiny bit frustrating. And Google’s solution appears to be just raising the screen brightness.
The folks over at Android Authority uncovered a new option being built out in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2 which is simply titled “Brighten screen in low light.” Google’s summary of the feature reads:
Automatically boost screen brightness so Face Unlock works in dim lighting.
Sounds fun in a dark room.
An assortment of strings related to the feature further detail what to expect, with Google seemingly set to offer granular settings around if the feature is used when Bedtime mode, Do Not Disturb, or driving is detected, as well as a setting to tailor just how bright the screen can get.
“Reliable” sounds like it might turn up the brightness higher to ensure an accurate reading from Face Unlock, while “Comfortable” seems to trade brightness for, well, not blinding you.

It still doesn’t sound like a particularly elegant solution, but it’s certainly better to have the option available. As for when Google might roll this feature out, that also remains to be seen.

articles.title_orig: Inside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: The New Game-Changing Tech Powering Every Mode
articles.title_zh: Inside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: The New Game-Changing Tech Powering Every Mode
articles.content_orig:
Infinity Ward recently opened its Krakow research and development centre to us to showcase the technical advancements powering Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Infinity Ward Poland studio head Michal Drobot was on hand to present debug footage that explained how current-gen hardware on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and PC enables unprecedented visual and systemic upgrades. While a Nintendo Switch 2 version is also launching in parallel via Digital Legends, the core engine focus remains firmly on pushing broader performance and graphical boundaries - including ray-marched smoke and fog, revamped rasterisation techniques informed by path tracing, and a comprehensively reworked animation and movement system.
Let's start with one of the standout additions, a brand new volumetric ray-marched smoke and fog system built exclusively for MW4. Working in tandem with traditional transparencies, this voxel-based solution allows players to interact directly with smoke plumes using gunfire or vehicles. Bullets carve precise temporary holes through the volume - as in Counter-Strike 2 - while sprinting characters displace wisps naturally, all operating within a fixed GPU performance ceiling.
This unified voxel framework extends seamlessly across atmospheric elements, height fog, and overhead clouds, ensuring consistent competitive balance across all online multiplayer and DMZ modes. Server and local client synchronisation guarantees that visual interactions such as lighting, shadows, and smoke dispersion appear identically for every participant. Furthermore, volumetric fog self shadows and interacts dynamically with animated light sources within the environment.
Weather systems also benefit heavily from the new voxel architecture, supporting dynamic transitions between sunshine, rainfall and snow across expansive open maps - a huge change for open-ended modes like DMZ. Snow layers accumulate dynamically on top of existing level geometry, allowing players to gradually reveal the original terrain beneath. Additionally, expanded character and object voxels now track more environmental states than previous games - a great range of variables that coats soldiers in mud, dust, blood or water streaks depending on their movement.
Next there's the new material workflow used in Modern Warfare 4. While full path tracing is reserved for internal visual reference only due to its heavy performance cost - and RT global illumination and RT reflections are PC-exclusive features - MW4 developers chose to heavily optimise rasterisation pipelines, achieving visual results remarkably close to path tracing at a fraction of the computational expense. This strategy ensures the game easily maintains a high frame-rate across a much wider spectrum of hardware, a key consideration given how much of Call of Duty's audience plays on console with 60fps in mind.
A core component of this improved rasterised approach is the neural light grid, which leverages machine learning compression to handle dynamic ambient occlusion and global illumination, a rethought approach that seeks to avoid the typical artefacts caused by screen-space reflections (SSR) and screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO). By storing lighting data more efficiently, light probes can be distributed sparsely across levels without sacrificing visual fidelity. Incidentally, it's an innovation that also helps to reduce the game's installation sizes alongside improved texture streaming techniques.
In part, material rendering receives a major upgrade through custom capture hardware known as the ATVI CT Reflectometer 2.0. By capturing physical surface properties across multiple light gradients, artists are able to access accurate bidirectional reflectance distribution function values for skin, clothing and metallic surfaces. This new material workflow integrates well with the enhanced rasterised ambient occlusion and global illumination passes.
Under the hood, significant optimisations target the entire rendering pipeline through advanced variable rate shading. Variable rate shading dynamically compresses visual data in less critical areas while preserving full native resolution where it matters most, drastically reducing overall graphical overhead - and this time, it's now applied throughout the entire render pipeline, not just for the final rendered pixels. Additional efficiency is gained through multi-resolution transparencies, with effects like smoke scaling in resolution based on distance.
Supporting these techniques, a hybrid rendering setup is also in place: combining traditional forward rendering (F+) with a visibility buffer (V+) for dense geometry. Where it's efficient to do so, parts of the scene will flip from one to the other, with F+ tending to handle triangles nearer the player.
Finally, foundational gameplay mechanics have been completely overhauled alongside these more visual-focused upgrades. Character movement directly influences weapon sway and contextual interactions with walls, while a new physical bullet trajectory simulation replaces older random bloom mechanics.
Together with these technical engineering achievements, Modern Warfare 4 stands as one of the more significant series milestones. It refines the experience for long term fans of the franchise - and impressions from the early access period suggest the campaign at least is one of the series' best in recent memory. We'll have more to say on Modern Warfare 4 to come, including the Switch 2 edition, but for now the outlook on the game's tech is promising to say the least.

articles.title_orig: NY congressional nominee Brad Lander says he was detained by the IDF in the West Bank
articles.title_zh: NY congressional nominee Brad Lander says he was detained by the IDF in the West Bank
articles.content_orig:
Lefty congressional nominee Brad Lander claimed Wednesday he was “detained” by the Israeli Defense Forces while working on an olive harvest in the West Bank.
Lander, the former Big Apple Comptroller who is running for Congress in the Nov. 3 election, posted a picture of himself glaring at the camera while onboard a bus with others who were on their phones and didn’t seem fazed.
“I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers,” Lander posted on X. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank.”
It is unclear if Lander, who is vying for New York’s 10th Congressional District seat, was doing anything else besides olive harvesting.
“The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know,” he added.
Lander had bested outgoing Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY) in their June primary, mounting a challenge against him from the left. Lander, who is Jewish, has been an outspoken critic of Israel.
During his primary against Goldman and his unsuccessful run for mayor last year, Lander made Israel a top issue.
The Dem candidate has opposed unconditional military aid to the Jewish state and accused it of carrying out a genocide in the Gaza Strip after the bloody Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack.
“I think — with deep sadness — that Israel’s conduct in Gaza meets the definition of genocide. But even if you don’t, it’s profoundly inconsistent with the Jewish value that every one of those Palestinian kids were created in the image of God, just like ours,” he posted on X in June.
Lander also contended that “Israel can’t be a genuine democracy while it’s occupying the West Bank & Gaza.”
Rabbis for Human Rights, an Israeli human rights group, corroborated Lander’s claim about being detained and said 90 other volunteers were held by the IDF as well, while harvesting olives in Nahalin, outside Bethlehem.
Authorities designated the area they were working in as a military zone closed for a full day, according to the group.
Officials then checked the group for identification, despite the group’s leaders offering to leave voluntarily, according to Rabbis for Human Rights’ version of events.
“We came to accompany farmers to land they have not been able to reach in three years, and after two hours of quiet harvesting, large forces arrived and closed the area,” Acting executive director for Rabbis for Human Rights, Anton Goodman, said in a statement.
“No one could have known about this order in advance. Instead of protecting people working their own land, the army is removing them from it, and detaining those who came to stand beside them.”
Lander previously described his venture to the West Bank as a mission to help Palestinians with their harvest and to put the spotlight on conditions there.
Other lefty pols have had similar run-ins with Israeli authorities. In July, for example, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said he and his group were detained by the Israelis for over an hour while in the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta during a tour.

articles.title_orig: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
articles.title_zh: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
articles.content_orig:
Fueled by the global boom in artificial intelligence stocks, relaxed capital rules and greater lending to hedge funds, big Wall Street banks have already had a banner year for equities trading — even with one quarter left to go.
The five biggest investment banks have generated about $67 billion in equities revenue through Sept. 30, according to company filings. That is $7 billion more than what the group made during all of 2025, which itself was a record haul.
But it's Wall Street's Big Three that have captured the largest slice of what is shaping up to be the industry's most lucrative arena: Goldman Sachs , JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley have made a combined $52 billion in stock trading revenue so far this year, nearly 80% of the total.
"When it comes to the AI mega trade, the Big Three consider each other their main competitors, and that's pretty much it," Mike Mayo , Wells Fargo banking analyst, told CNBC. "They've been best positioned to take advantage of this market."
Wall Street banks are experiencing an epic run of blockbuster profits as the total value of the stock market balloons and trading activity from institutional and retail investors rises across stocks, exchange-traded funds and derivatives. Helping drive this activity are the loans that the banks, through their prime brokerages, are extending to hedge funds so that they can amplify their bets.
Prime brokerage — the business of providing hedge funds with margin loans, securities lending and other trading services — has become a key battleground and source of growth. The Big Three's prime brokers are central to the larger equities story because they serve the largest funds across markets and products.
Demand for leverage to make bets on AI hardware, hyperscalers and chip suppliers has reached new heights, bank executives said last week.
At Goldman Sachs, equities financing activities jumped 96% in the third quarter to a record $3.37 billion. JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley don't break out that figure, but said they saw a similar dynamic.
"I like your 'insatiable demand for capital' point. That feels about right," JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said on the bank's third-quarter conference call, responding to analyst questions about financing demands.
"In this moment where AI is such an overwhelming theme ... there is capital being tapped through all kinds of different mechanisms," Barnum said.
That demand has helped transform equity desks at the Big Three from cyclical, transactional businesses into more durable, high-margin lending engines, Wall Street executives say.
The performance gap between Wall Street's giants and rivals including Bank of America and Citigroup highlights a widening divide in capital markets.
"For clients, the value isn't just a price on one trade, it's coverage and continuity," Rachid Alaoui, JPMorgan global head of equities, told CNBC in an interview. "You want a dealer that can give you the full suite across products, and you want that service to travel with you across regions. That matters in stressed markets and periods of volatility."
Executing multibillion-dollar bets, like leveraged swaps on volatile AI stocks or sector ETFs, can require an enormous balance sheet. The biggest banks can absorb potential $100 million losses without threatening their quarters, according to trading executives. Smaller or more niche banks can't underwrite single-trade risks of that magnitude, forcing them to decline the business or cede share.
U.S. prime brokers have also benefited from the retreat of European banks including Credit Suisse from the equities business, said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Herman Chan .
"Prime is one of the ultimate scale businesses," Chan said. "If you have a strong equities franchise, the hedge funds will want to transact with you because you have a bigger pool of trading opportunities with counterparties."
While U.S. markets were swept up in software and cloud computing giants this year, trading executives say the fastest-growing frontier for equities was in Asia.
Institutional investors poured into South Korea and Taiwan, targeting the "picks and shovels" of the AI supply chain: the memory chipmakers and semiconductor manufacturers supporting data center construction, Alaoui said.
For the Big Three, with their footprints across Tokyo; Hong Kong; Seoul, South Korea; and Mumbai, India; the Asia trade was a goldmine. However, trading executives point out that transaction taxes and stamp duties are included in top-line revenue, artificially inflating Asia prime totals.
There is also no agreed-upon definition of what equities trading revenue should include, so some banks include business lines like clearing services that others exclude from their stock trading totals, making apples-to-apples comparisons difficult.
But that doesn't change the overall momentum of the business, boosted by a stock rally that began in October 2022, weeks before OpenAI released ChatGPT.
"We're still in a stock-based world," Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick said on the firm's earnings call. "Equities are still, all things being equal, the attractive asset class."
While the CEOs of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley have said the AI build-out is still in its early years, if AI turns out to be not as transformative as hoped, a downturn could impact those banks more than others, analysts said.
The boom has also drawn some concern over the possible risks posed by hedge funds.
The International Monetary Fund warned this month that growing leverage , crowded positions and correlated selling from hedge funds could create potential stability risks. The IMF estimated that global hedge fund assets had reached $13 trillion.
In August, JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said industrywide leverage was "the highest it's ever been ," though he stopped short of calling the risk big enough to pose a threat to the financial markets.
Wall Street executives and analysts pointed out that the industry wasn't fazed by the meltdown of several hedge funds this summer. While the hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, Situational Awareness , garnered the most headlines, several smaller firms also experienced a forced unwinding.
Prime brokers have learned to leap on margin calls and quickly take down risk when markets move against clients, JPMorgan's Alaoui said.
"In the summer, some investors had positions they were forced to unwind," he told CNBC. "They deleveraged, risk came down, and the market moved on."
Another factor driving the equities boom: Trump administration regulators have eased some leverage rules for the largest U.S. banks, giving them more room to expand balance sheet-heavy businesses including prime brokerage. The revised rules were finalized in 2025, and banks were allowed to adopt them as early as January.
By easing the stringent balance sheet caps that previously treated Treasurys and prime brokerage loans, which are collateralized, the same as riskier assets, regulators gave dealers greater flexibility to deploy balance sheet capital.
"Capital did go down, so you have to say the system is somewhat more levered because of the relaxation in regulations," said Darrell Duffie , a finance professor at Stanford University and a leading expert on financial stability. "It's not a good idea, but it hasn't gotten dramatically out of whack."
The larger size of the market and higher volatility can create more trading, derivatives activity and leverage, he said, but that's not inherently alarming.
Wall Street executives also downplayed concerns over leverage, pointing out that they use collateral and frequent stress testing to get ahead of problems.
"Hedge fund leverage as a contributor of risk to the system is very much in the category of known unknowns," JPMorgan's Barnum said last week. "It doesn't mean it's riskless, but we kind of know what it is."

Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
A slice of Viking strategic combat right out of the heart of Scandinavia’s indie development scene, Bad North was at the vanguard of a wave of smart yet intrinsically accessible real-time strategy titles.
Swedish developer Plausible Concept calls it ‘micro-strategy’ and it's the perfect encapsulation of a minimalist approach that covers everything from unit management to the Monument Valley -style isometric art style.
With enough enemy variance to convince you you’re playing an interactive episode of the Vikings TV show, this endlessly entertaining sea of bitesize battles will teach you to fear — and love — the sound of the oncoming horde.
Balatro is a roguelike for gamers who don't like roguelikes... and then everybody else on top of that. It utterly nails what it sets out to do, providing an instantly accessible, satisfying, and addictive gameplay loop that anybody can grasp.
It's an immensely enjoyable experience from the start, but as you get deeper in, there's really nothing else quite like it. Sublime.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
In 2023, a year dominated by titanic, big-budget releases like Tears of the Kingdom and Mario Wonder , off-the-wall roguelike Dave The Diver stepped up to the plate and knocked the ball clear of the park with a heaving swing.
Its charming animations and writing supplement a mechanically dense experience that never stops dangling a new carrot to chase. You owe it to yourself to pick up this outstandingly funny, enthralling, and weird gem.
Death's Door is a modern classic, utilising old gameplay ideas in a new setting to make for a short and sweet experience you won’t want to miss. The snappy combat, rewarding exploration, and relaxing music will stick with you once you've finished, and while it may not have anything 'new' to offer, Death’s Door is so high quality that you’ll hardly have time to think about its lack of innovation.
Any fans of Zelda or Soulslike games will adore this - Acid Nerve has crafted an experience that’s absolutely worth your time and money.
An attractive art style, strong combat system, and meaningful player choices make Dicefolk a brilliant addition to the library, as it manages to feel fresh without getting too far away from the core ideas that make these sorts of games so addictive and popular.
Dicefolk is a good entry point to the genre, in fact; approachable without being patronising and it’s tons of fun once you get a grasp of it

articles.title_orig: How We Draw Lines in a World Awash in A.I. Images
articles.title_zh: How We Draw Lines in a World Awash in A.I. Images
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
I remember when AI images were easy to spot thanks to dead giveaways like freakishly mutated hands, warped faces, and Escher-like architecture. That was way back in 2023. Since then, things have progressed fast. AI image generators now are so good that it’s genuinely hard to tell what’s real and what isn’t.
But that doesn’t stop us humans from thinking we still have an eye for what’s real and what’s fake. So if you still think you’ve got it, then go ahead and give it a try with Slop Sense . It’s a free website with a handful of games that put your AI-detecting skills to the test.
My favorite game is called Reality Check where you’re shown an image and have to guess whether it’s a real photo or an AI-generated one. You get 10 seconds to make each guess and 60 seconds to rack up as many points as possible.
You’ll earn points for correct guesses, lose points for mistakes, and get bonuses for stringing together correct answers. When the timer runs out, you can go back through the images and see which ones tripped you up. It even provides the prompt used to generate the AI images. My score was shockingly abysmal at 12 out of 22 correct.
There’s also Ghostwriter, which takes the same idea but asks you to guess which text is written by AI and which is written by humans. I actually found this to be easier, but that may be because my job involves actually writing text all day.
These are a fun time waster and if nothing else, they’re an eye opening experience for how convincing AI-generated images and text are becoming—think about that the next time you’re mindlessly scrolling through social media confidently thinking you know what’s AI slop and what’s not.
Oh, and the irony of using AI to build games about spotting AI isn’t lost on me.
